chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Trimming the nails prevents the greatest illness and brings about livelihood.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of trimming nails according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Al-Kafi, this hadith links the physical act of nail trimming to both spiritual purity and material well-being, identifying the 'greatest illness' (al-daa' al-a'zam) as likely referring to leprosy or general disease, while also promising increased sustenance (rizq). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition), where maintaining bodily hygiene is viewed as an act of worship that invites divine blessings and protects against affliction.
